bonds.analysis:
Considering a 6-12 month time frame for the bond portfolio, we can implement a laddered maturity structure to achieve low-risk returns. Specifically, we'll aim to allocate bonds maturing in different years to minimize concentration risk. For a 6-12 month horizon, we can divide the portfolio into 4 maturity buckets: 3 months, 6 months, 9 months, and 12 months. To adhere to the 'no more than 30% maturing in any single year' constraint, we can allocate 20% to the 3 months bucket, 20% to the 6 months bucket, 20% to the 9 months bucket, and 20% to the 12 months bucket. This laddered structure will help distribute the maturities and minimize concentration risk.
  
  To maintain a diversified and low-risk portfolio, we will consider investment-grade corporate bonds. Companies like Microsoft (MSFT) and Johnson & Johnson (JNJ) are considered to be of high credit quality and can be considered for investment in a bond portfolio.
